answer: We deploy dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, fused with staking collateral and zero-knowledge verifiable delay to enforce cryptoeconomic primitives. Mapping identity multiplication to a walnut fleet docking at a cryptographic jetty within a bounded harbor, this capital barrier proves expected payoff of proliferation is strictly negative via severe slashing penalties. Thus, these mechanisms drive Nash equilibrium convergence in adversarial multi-agent environments, forcing rational actors to reject Sybil attacks.
